newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end off on more profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end off on more profit-taking.

text.p: Mexican stocks fell for the second straight session Thursday on profit-taking.

"The market is now slightly overbought, and is going through a stabilisation period which may be very short and pave the way for another rally," said Leonor Gonzalez, technical analyst at the BBV-Probursa brokerage.
The blue chip IPC index lost 13.87 points to 3,376.61. Volume was lackluster at 62.3 million shares traded.
"The market was listless, and volume was thin. I think it's because the holiday season has begun," said a trader. "I feel a few foreign dealers may have been drawn back to the Dow Jones."
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 14.16 points to 6,437.10.
In Mexico's broader market, losers outnumbered winners by 57 to 19.
Financial stocks had a choppy day. Traders said the sector has been volatile due to expect effects of applying international accounting rules to Mexican banks next year.
Financial stocks BBV Probursa and GFBital were first and fourth, respectively, on the gainers list, while another financial group, Serfin was a prominent loser.
BBV Probursa and GFBital gained one ($0.01) and ten centavos ($0.01), respectively, to 44 centavos ($0.06) and 5.50 pesos ($0.70). Serfin meanwell fell 15 centavos ($0.02) to 2.50 pesos ($0.32).
Analysts were cautiously optimistic the market was undergoing a consolidation after a strong rally on Tuesday.
"If we can weaken the 3,450-point level at heavy volume, then we could reach 3,650 points by the end of December or early January," said Gonzalez.
